After Close + full page reload, dialog does NOT reappear for parent4. Logging in as parent3 on /dashboard with court door shows court-celebration ONCE for them too; after Close + reload it does not re-show. Undo flow: with 6/6 agreed, clicking court-agree-undo-0 drops the label to '5 of 6 areas agreed', hides the 'All agreed' badge; re-agreeing (via API) back to 6/6 does NOT re-show the celebration for either parent. No horizontal overflow at 390 width (documentElement.scrollWidth<=clientWidth). All data-testids documented in review_request are present and correctly wired.
critical_code_review_comments: court_agreements.set_mark uses two update_one calls (one upsert with $addToSet, then a conditional clear of agreed_at when marked_by becomes empty). The latter cannot actually fire on the agreed=True branch (marked_by just got added); and on agreed=False the second update conditions on marked_by:{$size:0} which is correct — minor DX nit, consider a single pipeline update for atomicity when two parents race on undo.

AgreeControls disables the Save note button when note.trim() === row.note. The server stores a whitespace-collapsed version, but the component compares the raw textarea value against server-stored row.note. If a user adds trailing whitespace only, the save button looks enabled but a save with 'foo  ' == 'foo' server-side would not change anything; harmless, but could be surprising. Consider local .trim() in both sides of the equality check.

CourtCelebration useEffect schedules a setTimeout for the second confetti burst but does not cancel it in the StrictMode double-invoke case explicitly beyond the clearTimeout cleanup; fine today but a longer burst sequence should use a ref'd queue.

GET /compare/pdf — Content-Disposition filename is hard-coded ASCII only. If a parent's court_legal_name contains non-ASCII characters today they appear via FPDF _safe translit; the filename remains fixed, which is good; no issue.

Backend intent_notice is duplicated as a constant in court_agreements.py and used by the frontend via API payload — frontend never hardcodes it, which is correct (verified by locating court-celebration-notice value coming from compare.data.intent_notice). Keep it that way; do not inline the string in CourtCelebration.jsx.

For the PDF text extraction, FPDF multi_cell wraps the intent notice onto multiple lines so matching the ENTIRE sentence fails; match on 'evidenced their intent' and 'binding agreement' separately. For UI testing, use page.request (session cookies) rather than reading access_token from localStorage — the app does not store the JWT there (login uses httpOnly cookie); page.request inherits cookies and happily hits /api/court-path/compare* for setup. court-agree-{i}/court-agreed-{i} indices are NOT stable across parents (the difference list is caller-first), so scan 0..5 to find the current state. Celebration auto-opens via a useEffect in CourtOrderedView.jsx; closing it POSTs /compare/celebrated server-side (verified in test), so a reload will not reopen for that parent.
rca of the issue: No bugs found. One PDF-test calibration note: FPDF's multi_cell line-breaks the intent notice across 3-4 wrapped lines so the whole sentence does not survive as a single Tj in the content stream. Our test matches on two substrings that each live on a single wrapped line ('evidenced their intent' and 'binding agreement'). The user-visible PDF content is still the full sentence.
